title: Write jmap-chat-filenode-guide.md companion implementer guide
description:
Companion implementer guide for draft-atwood-jmap-chat-filenode-00, covering the operational and policy topics the filenode draft defers to deployments.

CONTEXT

The filenode draft (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-filenode-00.md, ~260 lines) binds a Space to a FileNode tree, defines the permission mapping for file operations, and addresses the Space-destruction grace period. Some operational topics are in the spec itself (the manage_channels-or-above permission mapping, the grace period default, the implicit-all-permissions controller bypass). What is NOT covered is the operating-a-file-storage-service view: how a deployment actually runs file storage at scale.

SCOPE (proposed)

Eight sections, each in the established 'what spec leaves open + what to decide + considerations + common patterns + recommended starting point' shape:

1. Storage backend choice
   - Local filesystem, S3-compatible object storage, dedicated file server, hybrid.
   - Durability, latency, cost tradeoffs.
   - Operational complexity per choice.

2. File type policy
   - Allowlists, denylists, MIME-type validation, magic-byte verification.
   - Executable handling (block? quarantine? signed-only?).
   - Archive expansion policies (zip-bomb defense).

3. Virus / malware scanning
   - When to scan: upload-time, download-time, periodic background.
   - Integration with scanning services (ClamAV, commercial APIs).
   - Action on detection: block, quarantine, flag, notify uploader, notify recipients.

4. Quota management
   - Per-Space, per-account, per-deployment quotas.
   - Soft vs hard limits.
   - Quota signaling to clients (the spec's overQuota SetError).
   - Storage-cost accounting.

5. Thumbnail and preview generation
   - Server-side vs client-side rendering.
   - Supported types (image, video, PDF, office docs).
   - Cache strategy and storage for derived previews.
   - Privacy: previews can leak content; consider end-to-end encrypted contexts.

6. Retention after Space destruction
   - The spec's grace period defaults (covered in filenode draft section 'Space Destruction').
   - Implementing the grace period in storage terms.
   - Restoration during grace period.
   - Hard-delete vs tombstone after grace expires.

7. Performance tuning
   - Caching strategy (local cache, CDN integration).
   - Range-request handling for large files.
   - Large-file streaming patterns.
   - Concurrent-upload handling.

8. Migration patterns
   - Moving file trees between storage backends without downtime.
   - Cross-region replication and read-from-replica considerations.
   - Backup and restore procedures.

WHAT THIS GUIDE DOES NOT NEED TO COVER

- The permission mapping itself: in the filenode draft directly.
- The grace-period mechanism: in the filenode draft directly.
- The controller-principal bypass: in the main draft (and is generic, not filenode-specific).
- The protocol itself: in draft-atwood-jmap-chat-filenode-00.md and draft-ietf-jmap-filenode-13.

WORK PLAN

Similar to fo22:
1. Skeleton with section headings and stubs.
2. Fill in sections in order; commit per major section.
3. Cross-reference into the implementer guide and the federation guide (file transfer across federation has its own considerations).
4. Final pass for consistency.

'A note on RFC 2119 keywords' wrapper mandatory.

P4: not urgent. Filenode deployments are emerging; the guide is parked aspirational. Promote priority when demand materializes.
acceptance_criteria:
- jmap-chat-filenode-guide.md exists at the top level of the repo.
- All eight proposed top-level sections (or a defensibly-revised set) are present and non-empty.
- Each topic section follows the established shape.
- 'A note on RFC 2119 keywords' wrapper at top.
- No content duplicated from filenode spec or other guides; cross-referenced instead.
- Cross-reference table at the bottom.
- AGENTS.md cross-file consistency table extended to include filenode-guide topics.
- Implementer-guide cross-reference table extended to include filenode-guide.
close_reason: Both companion guides written: jmap-chat-federation-guide.md (850 lines, 7 sections) and jmap-chat-filenode-guide.md (937 lines, 8 sections). Each section follows the established 5-subsection pattern. RFC 2119 wrapper present in both. Cross-reference tables added at the bottom of each guide. AGENTS.md cross-file consistency table extended. jmap-chat-implementer-guide.md cross-ref table extended.
